commons:98280862.summary: Christ, haloed and robed in red and blue, raises his hand toward the tomb, where Lazarus stands upright in his grave clothes, while a figure in red lies prostrate at Christ's feet. Crowds of onlookers fill the scene below a tall mountain and a turreted building. With its saturated colours and expressive figures, the Armenian miniature makes Christ's command, 'Lazarus, come forth', vivid and immediate.
facts: The Mughni Gospels (Matenadaran MS 7736) is an 11th-century Armenian Gospel book; Wikipedia dates it to 1060 and notes its 301 folios.
The miniature's Armenian caption reads 'The Resurrection of Lazarus' (per the Commons record).
commons:98280862.notes: The Commons title 'Mulna' refers to the Mughni (Mugni) Gospels, MS 7736, fol. 16v. The Commons Arabic description says 'end of the 11th century', while Wikipedia gives 1060.

europeana:2048087/ProvidedCHO_British_Mu.summary: This small cast crucifix, known here from the recording drawing, shows Christ in relief on the face of the cross, wearing a crown and a short skirt knotted at the waist, his arms apparently bound to the cross-arms. A broken suspension loop at the top shows that it was worn as a pendant. Found in Norfolk, it is a humble witness to personal devotion in late Anglo-Saxon England.
facts: The Portable Antiquities Scheme record compares its style with a silver crucifix from Gotland published by James Graham-Campbell in Viking Artefacts (1980) and with another find from the Isle of Wight.
The record describes the metal as worn and corroded to a purplish colour and dates the piece to the 11th century.
europeana:2048087/ProvidedCHO_British_Mu.notes: Description and date taken from the PAS record as served by Europeana; the PAS site itself blocked direct access. The worklist date '1000' was the aggregator's sort value; the record text says 11th century. The image is a line drawing, not a photograph.
